Review: Halden K4 burr grinder, bought from Brindle & Oak Home. Rating: 3/5

Let me start with the grinder itself, because it is genuinely excellent. The grind is consistent all the way from espresso-fine to French-press coarse, it's noticeably quieter than my old one, and retention is tiny: I weigh in 18 g of beans and get 17.9 g out. The packaging deserves real credit too: recycled cardboard, no plastic, and every part arrived intact.

Now, the 'Express 2-Day Delivery' I paid an extra $14 for. It arrived on day nine. Truly the fastest two days of my life. And a special shout-out to customer service, who answered my 'where is my order?' email with a lovely automated reply telling me to check the tracking page, the same tracking page that had said 'label created' for a week. Incredibly helpful, thank you so much.

Bottom line: buy the grinder, just don't count on it arriving when promised.

Subject: September close: vendor payments

Hi Mireille,

Quick status before Friday's close.

Payments: not a single one of the 42 vendor invoices due in September was left unpaid. The last two (Ostrander Print and Kelloway Logistics) cleared on 29 September.

Vendor contact: I can't say nobody complained, though. Kelloway's accounts-receivable contact called twice to complain that our remittance advice arrived late, even though the money itself landed on time.

Audit: it isn't untrue that the sampling turned up issues (three mis-coded expense lines), but none of them were material, and the auditors did not fail to sign off. The signed letter is in the shared drive under Close/2025-09.

Handover: I'm not unhappy to hand over the FX revaluation; Tomasz has agreed to take it on from October.

Best,
Aurelio

Ines,

I'm writing to give formal notice that Tarnwick Garden Supplies wants to terminate our freight agreement with Crossmere, effective at the end of this month.

This isn't a decision we've made lightly. Since June we've had three late deliveries to our Brackwell depot, including the August one that left us without stock for the bank-holiday weekend. Each time we were promised it wouldn't happen again. Each time, it did.

Regards,
Declan Moyo
Operations Director, Tarnwick Garden Supplies

Ines

state:
Wychcombe Road Community Garden: October newsletter

Harvest report
What a season. Between them, the shared beds produced just over 140 kg of potatoes, sixty-odd squashes and more runner beans than anyone could reasonably eat. Thank you to everyone who took bags down to the Aldous Street food bank; they tell us it was the most fresh veg they've had donated in a single month. The pumpkin patch did less well: slugs got to about half the plants in August, so next year we'll try copper tape and beer traps before resorting to anything stronger. The Tuesday children's group also found a grass snake sunning itself by the compost bays. Despite what some of them insisted, it was definitely not a python.

Work parties
Our autumn work parties are on the first and third Saturdays of the month, 10am to 1pm. The big jobs are clearing the bean frames, turning the compost bays and putting the greenhouse to bed for winter. No experience needed, and gloves are provided. If you can bring a fork or a wheelbarrow, even better.

Volunteer spotlight: Ruby Castellane
Ruby has been at Wychcombe Road since the very first spade went into the ground in 2016. She runs the seed library, teaches the Tuesday children's session, and is almost certainly the reason the herb spiral is still alive. This year she also rebuilt the rota spreadsheet that tells everyone whose turn it is to water. Thank you, Ruby. We genuinely don't know what we'd do without you.

Coffee morning
Our next coffee morning is on Sunday 19 October in the shed (weather permitting) or the church hall (weather not permitting). Pete from the Brew Barge has kindly donated a bag of his Java beans, and there will be cake. Donations go towards replacing the leaky water butt by the gate.

Plots and waiting list
We have two half-plots coming free in November. The waiting list is now on the garden's website rather than the paper sheet in the shed, so if you put your name on the old sheet, please add it online as well. At the moment there are nine people ahead of anyone joining today, so it may take a while.

Membership
Annual membership stays at £15 (£5 concessions) and is due by 1 April. You can pay in cash at any work party or by bank transfer; the details are on the noticeboard.

Reminders
Please don't leave tools out overnight; two spades went missing in September. The gate code changes on 1 November, and committee members will text the new code to everyone on the members' list.

See you in the mud,
The Wychcombe Road committee

PLOVER ANALYTICS: EXPORTING YOUR DATA (updated August 2026)

Overview. Plover lets you export tables, charts and dashboards in several formats. What you can export depends on your plan and on the size of the object you are exporting.

Large tables. The Export CSV button on a table view is capped at 1,000,000 rows. For larger tables, use Bulk Export, found under Settings > Developer > Bulk Export. Bulk Export writes compressed CSV files to your connected storage and emails you when the job finishes.

Formats. Tables can be exported as CSV or Excel, charts as PNG or SVG, and dashboards as PDF. CSV files use UTF-8 encoding with commas as separators; you can switch to semicolons under Settings > Workspace > Regional format.

Dashboards. Any dashboard can be exported as a PDF from the ••• menu in the top-right corner. PDF exports are limited to 50 pages; larger dashboards are split into several files automatically. PNG snapshots of individual charts can be downloaded by hovering over a chart and choosing Download image.

Scheduled exports. On the Growth and Enterprise plans you can schedule up to 10 recurring exports per workspace. Scheduled exports are delivered by email or to a connected S3 bucket. Starter plans cannot schedule exports.

API access. The REST API is available on all plans, with a limit of 600 requests per minute per workspace. Each request returns at most 10,000 rows; use the cursor parameter to page through larger results.

Spreadsheet exports. From any table view you can also export to Excel (.xlsx). Excel exports are limited to 100,000 rows because of spreadsheet size constraints, and they include only the columns currently visible.

Troubleshooting. If an export email doesn't arrive within 15 minutes, check your spam folder and confirm that the recipient address is verified under Settings > Notifications. Exports that fail three times in a row are paused until you edit and re-save them. Contact support@plover.example if a paused export keeps failing.

Data retention. Export files stored by Plover are kept for 30 days and then deleted automatically; files written to your own connected storage follow that storage provider's retention settings.

Audit log. Every export, including Bulk Export jobs, is recorded under Settings > Audit log with the user, the time and the row count.

state:
POST-INCIDENT REVIEW PIR-2291: checkout-api degradation (eu-west)
Status: Final. Author: Priya Nandakumar (Site Reliability). Reviewer: Tomasz Wierzba (Engineering Manager, Payments).

Summary
Between 09:12 and 10:47 UTC on 14 May, the checkout-api service returned elevated 5xx errors to roughly 18% of payment attempts in the eu-west region. The incident was declared SEV-2 at 09:26 UTC. No customer card data was exposed, and reconciliation found no duplicate charges.

Timeline (all times UTC)
08:55 CR-7710, a configuration change lowering the checkout-api database connection pool from 120 to 40 connections as part of a cost-reduction initiative, is deployed to eu-west. The change had been approved on 9 May.
09:12 Error-rate alarms fire for checkout-api in eu-west. The us-east deployment, which did not receive CR-7710, stays healthy throughout.
09:26 On-call engineer Lucas Ferrow declares SEV-2 and opens the incident channel.
09:30 Responders suspect an outage at the card processor, Carrowmere Payments. Carrowmere's status page shows no issues, and a test transaction routed through us-east succeeds.
10:10 Database dashboards show connection wait times above 3 seconds. The team identifies CR-7710 as the likely trigger.
10:18 Rollback of CR-7710 begins.
10:47 Error rates return to baseline; the incident is resolved.

Impact
About 4,300 checkout attempts failed during the incident window. Of these, an estimated 2,900 were retried successfully by the same customers within an hour. Finance's preliminary estimate of lost revenue is €61,000; the figure may be revised once the monthly reconciliation closes on 31 May. Separately, the search service had a brief latency spike at 09:48 UTC; it was unrelated to this incident and caused no failed requests.

Root cause
The reduced pool could not absorb the mid-morning traffic peak. Load tests for CR-7710 had been run only in staging, which carries roughly one-tenth of production traffic, so the pool never reached saturation before the change shipped.

What went well
- Alerting fired within one minute of the first errors.
- The rollback followed the documented procedure and completed in under 30 minutes.

What went poorly
- Roughly 40 minutes were spent investigating the card processor before anyone examined the database.
- The change record for CR-7710 did not include checkout-api's peak traffic figures, so reviewers had no basis for judging the new pool size.

Action items
1. Require production-scale load tests for any change that reduces connection-pool limits. Owner: Priya Nandakumar. Due 30 June.
2. Add a connection-saturation panel to the checkout-api on-call dashboard. Owner: Lucas Ferrow. Due 7 June.
3. Add peak traffic figures to the change-review template. Owner: Tomasz Wierzba. Due 14 June.

Follow-up
The cost-reduction initiative has been paused for all payment services until action item 1 is complete. A review of the initiative's remaining planned changes is scheduled for 2 July.

Drought-tolerant sorghum line shows promise in second season of trials

KESTREL VALLEY — Researchers at the Ambrose Institute for Dryland Agriculture say a new sorghum line, designated AIDA-S7, may offer farmers in semi-arid regions a more reliable harvest, though they stress that the results are preliminary and have not yet been peer-reviewed.

The trial, now in its second season, compares AIDA-S7 with Ochre Crown, the variety most widely planted in the region, across 36 plots at three sites: Kestrel Valley, Dunmore Flats and Oyelaran Station. Each site received roughly half its usual seasonal rainfall this year, which the team described as a useful stress test.

According to figures presented at a regional growers' meeting on 11 October, AIDA-S7 yielded an average of 2.7 tonnes per hectare across the three sites, compared with 2.1 tonnes for Ochre Crown. At Dunmore Flats, the driest site, the gap was wider: 2.3 tonnes against 1.4 tonnes. At Oyelaran Station the two varieties performed almost identically, a result the team attributes to an early-season hailstorm that damaged plots of both.

“We are encouraged, but two seasons is not enough to draw firm conclusions,” said Dr. Halima Osei-Brandt, who leads the project. “Yields swing a great deal from year to year, and we want at least one more season, ideally a wetter one, before we recommend anything to growers.”

The team also measured water-use efficiency. Preliminary analysis suggests AIDA-S7 produced about 18 percent more grain per millimetre of water than Ochre Crown, although soil-moisture sensors at Kestrel Valley malfunctioned for three weeks in July and the final figure may change once those gaps are dealt with.

Not every measure favoured the new line. AIDA-S7 plants were on average 12 centimetres shorter than Ochre Crown plants, which some growers at the meeting said could make mechanical harvesting harder. Grain protein content was slightly lower, at 10.8 percent compared with 11.2 percent for Ochre Crown. Taste panels organised by a local milling cooperative found no consistent preference between flours made from the two varieties.

The project is funded by a three-year grant of $1.4 million from the Tamberlin Agricultural Fund, which also supports a separate millet breeding programme at the institute. That programme, led by Dr. Viktor Anand, reported last month that its most advanced millet line had failed to outperform existing varieties and would be discontinued.

The team plans to submit the first two seasons of data to a peer-reviewed journal in the spring. A spokesperson said a small quantity of AIDA-S7 seed may be distributed to farmer cooperatives for demonstration plots next year, subject to approval by the national seed regulator. For now, AIDA-S7 seed is not sold commercially, and the institute has said it will not look for a commercial seed partner until the third season's results have been analysed.

Harlowmere Public Library, Board of Trustees
Minutes of the regular meeting held Tuesday 1 September, 6:30 p.m., Community Room

Present: Chair Doreen Valcourt; Vice-Chair Samuel Okafor-Reyes; Treasurer Ingrid Løvaas; Trustees Mateo Brandauer and Yuki Tanabe-Holm; Library Director Frances Adebayo-Lind. Absent: Trustee Colm Haverty.

1. Call to order and minutes
The Chair called the meeting to order at 6:34 p.m. The minutes of the 4 August meeting were approved as circulated (moved Okafor-Reyes, seconded Tanabe-Holm; carried 5–0).

2. Director's report
Director Adebayo-Lind reported that circulation in July and August totalled 41,200 items, up 6 percent on the same period last year. The summer reading programme enrolled 1,130 children, slightly below last year's 1,185. The Eastfold branch reopened on 19 August after carpet replacement, two days later than planned. Wi-Fi sessions at the main building have risen sharply since new access points were installed in June.

3. Treasurer's report
Treasurer Løvaas reported that year-to-date spending stands at 58 percent of the annual operating budget of $2.35 million, in line with projections. The county's contribution for next year has not yet been announced; the finance committee's draft budget assumes it will stay flat. Trustee Brandauer asked whether the energy savings from the new LED lighting could be quantified. Løvaas said she did not yet have figures and would bring them to the October meeting.

4. Roof replacement at the main building
Three bids were received for replacing the flat roof over the reading room. The Director recommended the bid from Quenby Roofing at $184,500, which was not the lowest. The lowest bid, from Fenwold Contractors at $171,000, excluded removal of the existing membrane, which staff estimated would add at least $20,000; the third bid, from Tarrow Building Services, was $226,000. Trustee Tanabe-Holm moved to accept the Quenby Roofing bid; Trustee Brandauer seconded. The motion carried 4–1, with Vice-Chair Okafor-Reyes voting against because of concerns about the project timeline. Work is expected to begin in October, weather permitting.

5. Public comment
Two residents spoke. One asked the board to consider restoring the Saturday evening study hall that was discontinued in 2023; the other thanked staff for the new English conversation groups.

6. Proposal to extend Sunday hours
The Director presented a proposal to open the main building from noon to 5 p.m. on Sundays beginning in January, at an estimated annual staffing cost of $38,000. Several trustees expressed support in principle, but the Treasurer asked that any decision wait until the county contribution is known. By consensus, the board tabled the proposal until the November meeting; no vote was taken.

7. Adjournment
The meeting adjourned at 8:02 p.m. The next regular meeting will be held on Tuesday 6 October.

question.instruction: Was circulation in July and August up 6 percent on the same period last year?

notes: Director's report: 41,200 items, up 6 percent on the same period last year.

Tollund Robotics beats revenue forecasts but trims full-year outlook

Tollund Robotics reported second-quarter revenue of $312.4 million on Thursday, up 9 percent from a year earlier and ahead of the $305 million analysts had expected, but the warehouse-automation company lowered its full-year forecast, citing delayed orders from two large logistics customers.

Net income for the quarter was $21.7 million, or 48 cents per share, compared with $26.3 million, or 58 cents per share, a year earlier. The company said higher component costs and a one-time charge of $6.1 million for folding its Werlingen assembly plant into its main facility weighed on profit.

Tollund now expects full-year revenue of $1.22 billion to $1.26 billion, down from its previous range of $1.28 billion to $1.32 billion. Chief financial officer Renata Sokolova-Hart told analysts on a conference call that the two delayed contracts, together worth about $70 million, had been pushed into next year rather than cancelled. “Neither customer has walked away,” she said. “The timing has moved, not the demand.”

Orders for the company's flagship picking arm, the T-400, rose 14 percent in the quarter, while orders for its older conveyor systems fell. Service and maintenance revenue, which the company has been trying to grow because it is steadier than equipment sales, reached $58 million, or about 19 percent of the total.

The results come a week after rival Corvane Motion reported a 3 percent decline in quarterly revenue, to $198 million, and said it would cut about 400 jobs. Tollund's chief executive, Anders Okwu-Lund, said on the call that Tollund had no plans for layoffs and would keep hiring engineers at its research centre in Aarvik, though more slowly than planned at the start of the year.

By region, revenue from North America, the company's largest market, grew 11 percent, while European revenue was roughly flat. Sokolova-Hart said she expects gross margin to recover in the second half as component prices ease, though she declined to give a specific target.

Shares of Tollund fell 7 percent in after-hours trading.

Analysts were divided. Priyanka Dessai of Harbourline Securities called the lowered guidance “prudent rather than alarming,” since the delayed orders had not been lost. Others pointed to rising inventory, which climbed to $240 million at the end of the quarter from $205 million three months earlier, as a sign that demand might be softening more broadly.

The company also said its board had approved a share buyback of up to $150 million over the next 18 months. It left its quarterly dividend unchanged at 12 cents per share.

Tollund is scheduled to report third-quarter results on 29 October.

Lake Orvanne Water Quality Monitoring: Summer Bulletin No. 3
Issued by the Orvanne Basin Authority, 28 August

This bulletin summarises results from samples collected between 1 and 21 August at the six public bathing sites on Lake Orvanne. Sampling followed the Authority's standard protocol: two samples per site per week, analysed at the Authority's laboratory in Pellisier within 24 hours of collection.

E. coli
The Authority's bathing-water standard is a single-sample maximum of 400 colony-forming units (CFU) per 100 mL. The highest single-sample result at each site during the period was:
- North Beach: 120 CFU/100 mL
- Cedar Point: 95 CFU/100 mL
- Marlow Cove: 410 CFU/100 mL (sample of 9 August; a resample on 10 August measured 60 CFU/100 mL)
- Heron Landing: 210 CFU/100 mL

VOLUNTARY RECALL NOTICE: Brisko KT-22 electric kettle

Halden Home Appliances is voluntarily recalling Brisko KT-22 electric kettles manufactured between 3 February and 28 April 2026, because the power-base connector can overheat and, in rare cases, melt. The company has received 14 reports of overheating, including two reports of minor burns to the hand. No fires have been reported.

Affected kettles have serial numbers beginning KT22-2602, KT22-2603 or KT22-2604; the serial number is printed on the underside of the power base. Kettles with serial numbers beginning KT22-2605 or later are not affected. The KT-20 model, which uses a different power base, is also not affected.

About 23,000 affected kettles were sold through department stores and online retailers between February and July 2026.

Customers should stop using the kettle immediately, unplug it, and contact Halden Home Appliances for a free replacement or a full refund. Customers do not need to return the kettle to the shop where they bought it; the company will post them a prepaid return label.

Structured light exposure to improve daytime sleep in night-shift nurses: a pilot randomised trial

Background: Night-shift nurses frequently report disrupted sleep, but few interventions have been tested in hospital settings. Methods: We conducted a pilot randomised trial at two hospitals in the Castellane health district. Sixty-two nurses working at least three night shifts per week were randomly assigned to a structured light-exposure schedule (n = 31) or usual practice (n = 31) for eight weeks. The primary outcome was total daytime sleep measured by wrist actigraphy. Results: Fifty-five participants completed the study (28 intervention, 27 control). Participants in the light-exposure group slept on average 34 minutes longer per day than controls (95% CI 9 to 59 minutes). Self-reported fatigue scores were lower in the intervention group, but the difference was not statistically significant. Two participants in the intervention group withdrew because of headaches. Conclusions: These preliminary findings suggest that a structured light-exposure schedule may increase daytime sleep among night-shift nurses. Because this was a small pilot, the results should be confirmed in a larger multi-site trial before the schedule is recommended for routine use. Funding: Castellane Nursing Research Council.

notes: 62 nurses were randomised, but only 55 completed the study.

Corrin Athletic 2–3 Veldhaven Rovers

Veldhaven Rovers came from two goals down to win at Quarry Meadow on Saturday, ending Corrin Athletic's seven-match unbeaten home run.

Corrin took the lead in the 12th minute when Tobias Achterberg headed in a corner from Luca Ferrante, and doubled it just before half-time with a Ferrante penalty after Veldhaven defender Samir Oduya handled on the line. Oduya was shown a yellow card rather than a red, to the fury of the home crowd.

Veldhaven manager Ingrid Castellanos made two changes at the break, and one of the substitutes, Kwame Aduayom, pulled a goal back in the 58th minute. Aduayom struck again in the 71st minute with a low shot from the edge of the area. The winner came in the 88th minute, when Rovers captain Henrik Vaalamo turned in Aduayom's cross at the far post.

Corrin thought they had equalised in stoppage time, but a second Achterberg header was ruled out for offside after a video review.

The result lifts Veldhaven to fourth in the table, two points behind Corrin, who drop to third. Attendance was 18,406.

POST-INCIDENT REVIEW — PIR-0419
Service: Checkout API, Brindlemoor Commerce
Incident date: Tuesday 14 May
Severity: SEV-2
Author: Oskar Lindqvist (SRE, on call)

Summary
Between 09:25 and 10:03 UTC the Checkout API returned HTTP 503 errors for a large share of requests (peaking at 58%). The trigger was a configuration change meant only for the staging cluster that was applied to production, where it lowered the database connection-pool limit on every checkout pod from 200 to 20. The resulting pool exhaustion went undetected by monitoring for 23 minutes because the relevant alert had been silenced during a maintenance window the week before and never re-enabled.

Timeline (UTC)
09:23 Config change CR-8812, intended for staging only, is applied to production because the deploy pipeline's environment selector defaulted to 'all'.
09:25 503 rate on /checkout rises from a baseline of 0.1% to 58%.
09:33 Customer Support receives the first tickets about failed checkouts.
09:48 The on-call engineer is paged manually by the support lead; the automated alert stays silent.
09:52 Dashboards show a traffic spike from a small set of IP ranges. The team suspects a DDoS attack and enables stricter rate limiting at the edge.
09:56 Rate limiting makes no difference and is switched off. Traffic analysis shows the spike is customers retrying failed checkouts, not an attack.
09:58 CR-8812 identified as the cause; rollback started.
10:03 Pool limit back at 200; error rate returns to baseline.

Root cause
The environment selector in the deploy pipeline defaulted to 'all' instead of forcing an explicit choice. Together with the silenced alert, this turned a harmless staging change into a production outage. CR-8812 itself was correct for staging and has since been re-applied there without issue. We investigated and ruled out the database servers (CPU and replication lag were normal throughout), the load balancers, and the DDoS hypothesis described above. A TLS certificate renewal that ran at 09:00 completed normally and is unrelated.

Customer impact
- Approximately 4,100 checkout attempts failed. Customers saw a generic error page, and no card was charged for a failed attempt.
- Some customers who retried had their order placed twice; 37 duplicate orders were identified and cancelled with full refunds by 16:00.
- No data was lost or corrupted; order history and saved baskets were unaffected.
- Login, search and browsing were not affected.

What went well
Support escalated quickly, and the rollback itself took under five minutes.

What went poorly
The silenced alert, above all. In addition, the stricter edge rate limiting enabled at 09:52 blocked some legitimate customer retries for the four minutes it was active.

Action items
1. Make the environment selector mandatory, with no default. Owner: Deploy Tooling. Status: Done (merged 16 May).
2. Give every alert silence an automatic expiry (maximum 72 hours). Owner: Observability. Status: In progress.
3. Add idempotency keys to checkout requests so that retries cannot create duplicate orders. Owner: Checkout team. Status: Not started.
4. Audit all currently silenced alerts. Owner: Observability. Status: In progress (about half reviewed).
5. Write a runbook for telling retry storms apart from DDoS traffic. Owner: SRE. Status: Not started.

SLA impact
The Checkout API carries a 99.9% monthly availability commitment, which the contract defines as no more than 43 minutes of unavailability per calendar month. An incident's unavailability is counted from the moment the error rate leaves baseline until it returns to baseline. Earlier this month, PIR-0411 caused 11 minutes of Checkout API unavailability. The 20-minute Search API outage on 6 May (PIR-0415) falls under a separate commitment and does not count here.

question.instruction:
According to the review, which of these contributed to the outage?
Options (any number can be correct, possibly none):
- An alert that should have caught the problem had been silenced
- A problem with a TLS certificate or its renewal
- A failure or overload of the database servers
- A configuration change was wrong even for the environment it was written for
- A configuration change was applied to an environment it was not meant for
- A distributed denial-of-service attack

A configuration change was applied to an environment it was not meant for
A failure or overload of the database servers

1. Make the environment selector mandatory, with no default. Owner: Deploy Tooling. Status: Done (merged 16 May).
2. Give every alert silence an automatic expiry (maximum 72 hours). Owner: Observability. Status: In progress.
3. Add idempotency keys to checkout requests so that retries cannot create duplicate orders. Owner: Checkout team. Status: Not started.
4. Audit all currently silenced alerts. Owner: Observability. Status: In progress (about half reviewed).
5. Write a runbook for telling retry storms apart from DDoS traffic. Owner: SRE. Status: Not started.

SLA impact
The Checkout API carries a 99.9% monthly availability commitment, which the contract defines as no more than 43 minutes of unavailability per calendar month. An incident's unavailability is counted from the moment the error rate leaves baseline until it returns to baseline. Earlier this month, PIR-0411 caused 11 minutes of Checkout API unavailability. The 20-minute Search API outage on 6 May (PIR-0415) falls under a separate commitment and does not count here.

notes: Outage ran 09:25–10:03 (38 min); with PIR-0411's 11 min that is 49, over the 43-minute limit. Search outage excluded.

INCIDENT REPORT — Halvorsen Distribution, Site 3
Report no.: HS-2291
Incident: Monday 9 June, approx. 14:40
Report filed: Wednesday 11 June, 09:15
Reported by: Callum Reid (shift supervisor)

Description: While reversing out of aisle 14, a counterbalance forklift driven by operator J. Sato struck the corner of a pallet-racking upright. The upright was visibly bent; the bay was taped off and unloaded as a precaution. A picker, A. Nowak, was standing about a metre behind the forklift as it reversed; she stepped aside just in time and was not struck. She reported no injury and finished her shift; the operator was also unhurt. The operator was wearing a hi-vis vest, safety boots and gloves, but not his seat belt. No stock fell from the racking.

Immediate actions: Bay 14-C closed; racking inspection requested from the manufacturer; operator stood down pending refresher training.

Site policy extract (H&S Manual §4.2):
- Any incident involving powered equipment must be reported within 24 hours.
- 'Near miss': a person could reasonably have been hurt but was not.
- 'Property damage': any damage to buildings, racking, vehicles or stock.
- 'PPE breach': a worker was not wearing required personal protective equipment, i.e. hi-vis vest, safety boots and, for forklift operators, gloves. Seat-belt use is covered by the §6.1 vehicle rules and is not a PPE matter.
- 'Externally reportable': only if someone was injured and off work for more than 7 days.

Link domain blocked at the web proxy. No sign-ins to Imogen's account from unusual locations or devices; password reset not required. Ravi's mailbox checked: message found in Deleted Items, never opened.

Aldercrest Vireo 14 — long-term review
Original rating: ★★★★★ | Updated rating: ★★★☆☆ (see the update at the bottom)

I bought the Vireo 14 in March to replace a five-year-old ultrabook, mostly for writing, spreadsheets and the occasional photo edit. I paid €1,149 for the 16 GB / 512 GB model.

Build and design. The aluminium chassis feels solid and there's almost no flex in the keyboard deck. At 1.3 kg it's easy to carry around all day. I'd read several forum threads about hinges cracking on early units, so I checked mine carefully when it arrived: it's firm with no creaking, and it still is today.

Screen. The 14-inch OLED panel is gorgeous — punchy colours and deep blacks. A friend bought the same model a week after me and his arrived with two dead pixels near the top edge, which meant sending it back; mine has been flawless. The glossy coating does reflect a lot outdoors, but that's the trade-off.

Keyboard and trackpad. Comfortable, with decent travel and a crisp feel. The trackpad is large and accurate, and the backlight has three levels.

Performance. Day to day it's quick. Photo exports are slower than on my desktop, obviously, but fine for my needs. The fan does come on under heavy load; it's a soft whoosh rather than a whine, and it's silent while I'm writing.

Battery. I was getting 10–11 hours of mixed use in the first months, which is excellent. It charges from either USB-C port.

Ports and speakers. Two USB-C ports, one USB-A port, a headphone jack and a microSD slot, which is more than most rivals offer at this size. The speakers are fine for video calls but thin for music, so I mostly use headphones. The 1080p webcam is perfectly adequate.

Software. Very little bloatware; I uninstalled a trial antivirus and a game launcher and that was it.

UPDATE, July (four months in)
Two things went wrong in quick succession. First, the 'E' key stopped registering unless I pressed it very hard. Then, about two weeks later, I noticed the trackpad lifting at its front edge — the battery underneath had swollen. I stopped using the laptop immediately.

Aldercrest support were polite and quick to respond. They confirmed both faults were covered by the warranty and arranged a courier pickup for a free repair (new battery and keyboard deck). I asked whether they would refund me instead; they declined, saying refunds are only available within 30 days of purchase. The repair took nine days and the laptop has been fine since, but I've knocked two stars off, because a swollen battery after four months is not acceptable at this price.

Q3 ENTERPRISE ACCOUNT HEALTH SUMMARY — Customer Success, Lumora HR Cloud
Prepared for the account-health meeting on 2 October

This summary covers the five enterprise accounts reviewed at the meeting and reflects their position as of 30 September.

1. Castellan Foods (ARR €410k; renewal 31 March)
In September Castellan's HR director, Ilse Brandt, raised two issues: payroll exports to their accounting system were failing roughly once a week, and they asked for a Portuguese-language interface for their Lisbon staff, which the product does not yet have. Engineering shipped a fix for the export failures on 19 September, and there have been no failures since. A Portuguese interface is on the roadmap for next year but has no committed date. Ilse mentioned that a competitor, Tessaly, had approached them, but said they have 'no plans to switch'. Castellan is opening a site in Porto and has asked for a quote for 300 additional seats. Overall sentiment: positive.

2. Brightwater Logistics (ARR €265k; renewal 15 November)
Brightwater's usage fell 40% over the quarter after their internal champion, Colm Treacy, left the company in July; nobody has taken over ownership of the platform. Their finance team has twice asked for an itemised invoice breakdown, which we have not yet provided. They have not reported any product defects. Their procurement lead told us they are 'running an RFP and evaluating alternatives before renewal'. Overall sentiment: negative. Flagged as at risk.

3. Norrvik Engineering (ARR €180k; renewal 30 June)
Norrvik reported slow load times on the scheduling module during their July peak, with pages taking 8–12 seconds. Performance improvements were deployed on 2 August, and in September Norrvik confirmed that load times are now under two seconds. They also asked for single sign-on with their identity provider, something the product already supports; we sent the configuration guide and SSO went live on 25 September. No commercial concerns were raised. Overall sentiment: positive.

4. Oriel Dental Group (ARR €95k; renewal 28 February)
Oriel's operations manager, Femi Adeyemi, is frustrated that leave balances are calculated incorrectly for part-time staff, an open defect (LUM-4410) that has now been outstanding for 11 weeks. Femi has asked for a service credit covering the months the defect has been open, and for a named account manager instead of the pooled support model. Overall sentiment: negative, though there is no sign they are considering leaving.

5. Saltmarsh Retail (ARR €320k; renewal 1 May)
No issues raised this quarter. Saltmarsh's CFO praised the new expenses module at their September business review and agreed to act as a reference customer. Overall sentiment: very positive.

Actions agreed
- Brightwater: arrange an executive-sponsor call by 20 October; send the itemised invoice by 10 October.
- Oriel: escalate LUM-4410 to engineering leadership; decide on the service credit by 15 October.
- Castellan: send the Porto seat quote by 9 October.
- Saltmarsh: add to the reference programme.
- Norrvik: no action needed.

Issue #3187 — CSV import silently drops rows containing accented characters
Opened by: kjell-l · Labels: bug

Environment: Ledgerly v4.8.2, self-hosted; server OS and database unchanged since the upgrade. The same import worked correctly on v4.7.3.

Steps to reproduce
1. Prepare a UTF-8 CSV file with 1,000 supplier rows, about 50 of which have accented characters in the name (e.g. 'Café Lumière', 'Øresund Trading').
2. Import it via Settings → Data → Import CSV.

Expected: 1,000 rows imported.
Actual: 953 rows imported. The import summary says 'Import completed successfully' and shows no warnings. The missing rows are exactly the ones with accented characters.

Other notes
- The rows that do get imported look correct: no mangled or altered values, just missing rows.
- The import takes about the same time as before (~4 s for 1,000 rows).
- As far as I can tell this isn't a security issue.
- Stripping accents before import works around it, but we can't do that with customer-facing names.
- Happy to test a fix on our staging instance.

@maintainers: this is blocking our migration — would appreciate a look before the 4.9 release.

Section 4. Eligibility. An employee qualifies for 16 weeks of paid parental leave only if all four conditions below are met.
4.1 Tenure: on the expected date of birth or placement, the employee has been directly employed by Brightwater for at least 12 continuous months. Time spent working at Brightwater through a staffing agency does not count toward tenure.

Saltmarsh Row Apartments - Residential Lease, Section 12 (Rent and Security Deposit)
12.1 Rent is due on the 1st day of each month. If the Tenant pays rent more than 5 days after the due date, the Tenant owes a late fee of $40.
12.2 Within 21 days after the Tenant moves out and returns all keys, the Landlord must either refund the full security deposit or send the Tenant an itemized statement of deductions together with the remaining balance.
12.3 If the Landlord misses the 21-day deadline in 12.2, the Landlord loses the right to make any deductions and must refund the entire deposit.
12.4 Permitted deductions are limited to unpaid rent, unpaid fees, and damage beyond normal wear and tear.

Property manager's notes: Tenant Ruth Okafor paid her July rent on July 10. She moved out on July 31 and handed in all keys the same day. Her security deposit was $1,500. On August 26 the Landlord, Marcus Bell, mailed Ruth an itemized statement deducting $300 for carpet cleaning and $40 for the July late fee, together with a check for $1,160.

question.instruction: Under the lease, does the landlord owe a late fee?

notes: Clause 12.1 late fees are owed by the tenant; the landlord's missed deadline only forfeits deductions under 12.3.

WAYVANE TRIP PROTECTION - Policy Wording, Plan TP-Gold (policies purchased on or after 1 September 2025)

PART A - DEFINITIONS
Trip cost: the prepaid, non-refundable payments for travel arrangements that the insured declared when buying this policy.
Travel companion: a person booked on the same itinerary as the insured.
Immediate family member: a spouse or domestic partner, parent, child, sibling or grandparent of the insured.
Pre-existing condition: any illness, injury or medical condition for which the insured received diagnosis, treatment or medication during the 60 days immediately before the policy purchase date.

PART B - SUMMARY OF COVER
Trip cancellation: up to 100% of trip cost.
Cancel For Any Reason (CFAR) rider, optional: up to 75% of trip cost. The rider can only be added if the policy is bought within 14 days of the first trip payment.
Baggage delay: up to $300 for essential purchases after a delay of 12 hours or more.
Emergency medical expenses: up to $50,000 per insured.

PART C - DECLARING MEDICAL CONDITIONS
When buying this policy, the insured must declare every pre-existing condition. A declared pre-existing condition is covered only if the insured also pays the medical screening premium shown in the quote.

PART D - HOW CANCELLATION CLAIMS ARE DECIDED
The claims team applies the rules below in the order listed. The first rule that applies decides the claim, and no later rule is considered.
Rule 1. If the claim is submitted more than 90 days after the date the trip was cancelled, the claim is denied.
Rule 2. If the cancellation results from a pre-existing condition that was not declared under Part C, the claim is denied.
Rule 3. If the trip was cancelled because of (a) sickness or injury of the insured or a travel companion, certified in writing by a physician as preventing travel, (b) the death of an immediate family member, or (c) an official evacuation order covering the destination, the insurer reimburses 100% of trip cost.
Rule 4. If the insured holds the CFAR rider and cancelled more than 48 hours before the scheduled departure, the insurer reimburses 75% of trip cost.
Rule 5. In all other cases, the claim is denied.

PART E - DOCUMENTS
A cancellation claim must include the booking invoice, proof of cancellation from each travel supplier, and any supporting medical or official documents. Missing documents delay a decision but do not change which rule applies.

CLAIM FILE MTP-26-04417
Insured: Tomasz Wierzbicki. Plan TP-Gold with CFAR rider, purchased 3 January 2026; first trip payment made 28 December 2025. Pre-existing conditions declared at purchase: none.
Trip: 10-day guided walking holiday in Madeira for two, departing 20 March 2026. Declared trip cost: $4,200.
Adjuster notes: The insured's brother, Pawel, was booked on the same itinerary but holds a separate policy with another insurer; his claim is not part of this file. On 15 December 2025 the insured strained his lower back while moving furniture and was treated by a physiotherapist the same day; he had no further treatment or medication for it until March 2026. He reports that his back felt fine through January and February and that he kept up his training walks. On 9 March 2026 the pain returned severely. On 10 March his physician, Dr. Anneliese Roth, certified in writing that he was unfit to travel because of a recurrence of the back strain. He cancelled the trip with the tour operator on 11 March 2026 and submitted this claim on 2 April 2026, attaching the physician's letter, the booking invoice and the operator's cancellation confirmation. The operator refunded nothing, so the full $4,200 is claimed.

question.instruction:
Which outcome do the Part D rules prescribe for claim MTP-26-04417?
Options (exactly one is correct):
- 100% of trip cost reimbursed under Rule 3
- Denied under Rule 5 (no earlier rule applies)
- Denied under Rule 1 (claim submitted too late)
- 75% of trip cost reimbursed under Rule 4 (CFAR rider)
- Denied under Rule 2 (undeclared pre-existing condition)

candidates.description: Denied under Rule 1 (claim submitted too late)
Denied under Rule 2 (undeclared pre-existing condition)
100% of trip cost reimbursed under Rule 3
75% of trip cost reimbursed under Rule 4 (CFAR rider)
Denied under Rule 5 (no earlier rule applies)

notes: Back strain treated 15 Dec 2025, 19 days before purchase, and undeclared; Rule 2 applies first, so Rules 3 and 4 are never reached.

Trip cost: the prepaid, non-refundable payments for travel arrangements that the insured declared when buying this policy.
Travel companion: a person booked on the same itinerary as the insured.
Immediate family member: a spouse or domestic partner, parent, child, sibling or grandparent of the insured.
Pre-existing condition: any illness, injury or medical condition for which the insured received diagnosis, treatment or medication during the 60 days immediately before the policy purchase date.

PART B - SUMMARY OF COVER
Trip cancellation: up to 100% of trip cost.
Cancel For Any Reason (CFAR) rider, optional: up to 75% of trip cost. The rider can only be added if the policy is bought within 14 days of the first trip payment.
Baggage delay: up to $300 for essential purchases after a delay of 12 hours or more.
Emergency medical expenses: up to $50,000 per insured.

PART C - DECLARING MEDICAL CONDITIONS
When buying this policy, the insured must declare every pre-existing condition. A declared pre-existing condition is covered only if the insured also pays the medical screening premium shown in the quote.

PART D - HOW CANCELLATION CLAIMS ARE DECIDED
The claims team applies the rules below in the order listed. The first rule that applies decides the claim, and no later rule is considered.
Rule 1. If the claim is submitted more than 90 days after the date the trip was cancelled, the claim is denied.
Rule 2. If the cancellation results from a pre-existing condition that was not declared under Part C, the claim is denied.
Rule 3. If the trip was cancelled because of (a) sickness or injury of the insured or a travel companion, certified in writing by a physician as preventing travel, (b) the death of an immediate family member, or (c) an official evacuation order covering the destination, the insurer reimburses 100% of trip cost.
Rule 4. If the insured holds the CFAR rider and cancelled more than 48 hours before the scheduled departure, the insurer reimburses 75% of trip cost.
Rule 5. In all other cases, the claim is denied.

PART E - DOCUMENTS
A cancellation claim must include the booking invoice, proof of cancellation from each travel supplier, and any supporting medical or official documents. Missing documents delay a decision but do not change which rule applies.

CLAIM FILE MTP-26-04417
Insured: Tomasz Wierzbicki. Plan TP-Gold with CFAR rider, purchased 3 January 2026; first trip payment made 28 December 2025. Pre-existing conditions declared at purchase: none.
Trip: 10-day guided walking holiday in Madeira for two, departing 20 March 2026. Declared trip cost: $4,200.
Adjuster notes: The insured's brother, Pawel, was booked on the same itinerary but holds a separate policy with another insurer; his claim is not part of this file. On 20 October 2025 the insured strained his lower back while moving furniture and was treated by a physiotherapist the same day; he had no further treatment or medication for it until March 2026. He reports that his back felt fine through January and February and that he kept up his training walks. On 9 March 2026 the pain returned severely. On 10 March his physician, Dr. Anneliese Roth, certified in writing that he was unfit to travel because of a recurrence of the back strain. He cancelled the trip with the tour operator on 11 March 2026 and submitted this claim on 2 April 2026, attaching the physician's letter, the booking invoice and the operator's cancellation confirmation. The operator refunded nothing, so the full $4,200 is claimed.

question.instruction: Under the policy wording, will Tomasz be reimbursed 100% of his trip cost?

notes: Rules 1 and 2 do not apply; Rule 3(a), a physician-certified injury of the insured, gives 100% of trip cost.

Linden Court Housing Cooperative - Allocation Committee packet, September 2026

VACANCY NOTICE
Unit 4B, a two-bedroom ground-floor apartment with a roll-in shower and widened doorways, becomes vacant on 1 September 2026. The previous residents have moved to a care facility, and the unit has been repainted.

ALLOCATION POLICY (adopted 2024, amended February 2026) - excerpt
1. Purpose. This policy sets out how vacant cooperative units are offered to people on the waitlist, fairly and transparently.
2. Joining the waitlist. Households must have an annual income at or below 80% of the area median income and must attend the cooperative's orientation session.
3. Order of offers. When a unit becomes vacant, the Allocation Committee offers it in the following order.
3.1 Accessible units. A unit with a roll-in shower or other wheelchair-accessible features must first be offered to applicants who require a wheelchair-accessible unit, regardless of tier. If there is more than one such applicant, the earliest application date goes first.
3.2 Priority tiers. Otherwise, offers follow these tiers:
Tier 1 - households displaced by a declared disaster within the 12 months before the vacancy date;
Tier 2 - current Linden Court residents requesting a transfer for a documented medical need;
Tier 3 - households that include a member aged 65 or older;
Tier 4 - all other applicants.
A household that fits several tiers is placed in the highest (lowest-numbered) tier.
3.3 Within a tier, the earliest application date goes first.
4. Declined offers. An applicant who declines two offers moves to the bottom of their tier.
5. Pets. Cats and small dogs are allowed with the committee's written consent; applicants must disclose pets when an offer is made.
6. Appeals. Applicants may appeal an allocation decision in writing within 14 days.

WAITLIST EXTRACT (applicants currently eligible for a two-bedroom unit)
WL-07 - Halvorsen household. Applied 3 January 2025. Household: Erik and Maja Halvorsen and Maja's mother, age 71. They rent privately in Eastfield. No accessibility needs reported.
WL-12 - Mr. Samuel Oduya. Applied 20 August 2025. Current Linden Court resident (Unit 2A, third floor) requesting a transfer; a letter from his cardiologist documents that he can no longer manage stairs. He walks with a cane and does not use a wheelchair.
WL-19 - Pereira household. Applied 1 November 2024. Household: Luis and Carla Pereira, both in their thirties, and their two young children, now renting a short-term apartment in Millbrook. Their previous home was destroyed on 12 June 2025 by the Millbrook River flood, a declared disaster. No accessibility needs reported.
WL-23 - Ms. Irene Castellanos. Applied 9 September 2025. Age 44, lives alone and rents privately across town. She uses a wheelchair full-time and requires a wheelchair-accessible unit.

COMMITTEE MEMBER NOTE
'The Pereiras have been on the list the longest and lost everything in the flood. I'd like us to offer them 4B.' - Doug Farrow, committee member

Voltara Electronics - Limited Warranty summary for support agents
1. Coverage. Voltara will repair or replace, free of charge, a device that fails because of a manufacturing defect within 12 months of the original purchase date.
2. Proof of purchase. A receipt or a Voltara order number is required for every claim.
3. Accidental damage. Drops, cracked screens and liquid exposure are not covered by this warranty. Customers who bought VoltCare+ may claim accidental damage for a $49 service fee, up to two claims in any 12-month period.
4. Unauthorized service. The warranty is void if the device has been opened or repaired by anyone other than Voltara or a Voltara-authorized service center.
5. Agent conduct. Agents must not promise outcomes that this summary does not allow, and should escalate unclear cases to a team lead.

Agent Sam: Sorry to hear that, Noor! Let's get this sorted. Could you share your order number or receipt?

Agent Sam: Thanks! I can see that order - the phone was purchased on 14 November 2025.
Noor Haddad: ok good. honestly the port has felt a bit loose since the first week
Agent Sam: Got it. Has the phone been dropped or exposed to water or other liquids?
Noor Haddad: no drops, it's always in a case. it got a little damp in my bag in the rain once but it worked fine after that

Noor Haddad: yes, three different cables, same thing. wireless charging doesn't work either
Agent Sam: That's helpful. Is there any visible damage to the port, like bent pins or debris?
Noor Haddad: not that i can see
Noor Haddad: out of curiosity, if i had bought VoltCare+ when i got the phone, would this be covered no matter what?
Agent Sam: I'll note that question for the team. One more check before I file the claim: has the phone ever been opened or repaired by anyone?
Noor Haddad: oh - my brother-in-law runs a phone repair kiosk at the mall. he took the back cover off last saturday to clean out the charging port, but he didn't replace anything
Agent Sam: Thanks for telling me. Is his kiosk a Voltara-authorized service center?
Noor Haddad: no, it's his own independent shop
Agent Sam: Understood. I'm passing this to my team lead for a decision and will email you within 24 hours.

question.instruction: Under the warranty summary, is Noor entitled to a free repair or replacement?

notes: Clause 4: the phone was opened by an independent, non-authorized kiosk, which voids the warranty.

TIDEWELL SCHEDULING — SUPPORT ROUTING RULES (v3, effective 1 March 2026)

Apply the rules in order. The first rule that matches a ticket decides its queue; later rules are not considered.

Rule 1 — Security. Any ticket that reports a suspected data breach, leaked or stolen login credentials, or unauthorised access to an account goes to the Security Desk, whatever else the ticket contains.

Rule 2 — Refunds. Refund requests for $250 or less go to Tier 1 Billing. Refund requests for more than $250 go to Finance Review. Exception: if the customer's account was created fewer than 30 days before the date the ticket was received, the refund request goes to Tier 1 Billing whatever the amount, because it is covered by our 30-day money-back guarantee.

Rule 3 — Outages and bugs. If the product is unavailable for more than 50 of the customer's users, route to the Incident Bridge. Outages affecting 50 users or fewer, and all other bugs, go to Tier 2 Technical.

Rule 4 — Everything else (how-to questions, feature requests, feedback) goes to the General Queue.

Notes for agents: do not use the ticket's subject line or the priority chosen by the customer to decide routing. The customer's plan (Starter, Growth or Enterprise) does not affect routing.

Definitions: a refund request is any ticket asking for money back, including a cancellation that asks for money back. Users affected means the number of the customer's users that the ticket says cannot use the product. Account age is measured from the account creation date shown in the ticket header.

Subject: My stay at the Vantaro Harbourside, 3–7 September

Dear Vantaro Customer Care,

I've just got back from four nights at the Vantaro Harbourside for the Nordic Logistics Summit, and I wanted to write while it's all still fresh.

First, the good parts, because there were plenty. The check-in team were lovely (Joanna upgraded me to a harbour-view room without my even asking), and the breakfast buffet was the best I've had at any conference hotel this year. The gym was clean and never crowded, and the concierge somehow found me a table at a seafood restaurant that was supposedly booked out for weeks. Please pass on my thanks to all of them. The conference facilities were excellent too: the summit organisers had the Lighthouse Suite for the main sessions, and your AV team sorted out a projector problem on the first morning in under five minutes. Lunch was served on time every day, which at a 300-person event is no small achievement.

The less good part: on the second night there was a wedding party in the courtyard below my room until well after 1am. I rang reception, who were apologetic and sent up earplugs, which helped a little. I'm mentioning it for your records rather than to complain. These things happen at busy hotels, and I'm not asking for any kind of compensation.

Now, the thing I actually need help with. My employer only reimburses travel against an invoice that shows the company's name and VAT number. The invoice I was handed at checkout is made out to me personally and has no VAT number on it, so our finance team has rejected my expense claim. They have confirmed that the amount itself is correct; only the name and VAT details need to change. Could you please reissue the invoice for the whole stay (folio 55-20931, total €1,248.60) addressed to:

Tidemark Haulage Ltd
VAT number: IE 3345127KH
14 Quay Street, Galway

Our expense deadline is the 30th, so the sooner the better.

A couple of other small things, just so you have the whole picture. I thought I'd left my laptop charger plugged in beside the desk, but it turned up in the lining of my suitcase when I unpacked, so there's no need to search the room. And I've checked that my Vantaro Circle points for the stay have posted: all 4,990 of them are there, so no action is needed on that either.

I'm already planning to come back for next year's summit, and I'll book directly with you once the dates are announced. Thanks again to the whole team; apart from the one noisy night, it was a genuinely lovely stay.

Kind regards,
Helena Marsh

From: Sunita Rao (Support Engineer, Cobaltix Cloud)
Sent: Mon 31 Aug 2026, 10:47

Hi Renata,

I've picked up the 502s under ticket CBX-58214. In the load balancer logs, the errors line up with upstream connections being closed by your instances while requests are still in flight. The most common cause is a mismatch between the load balancer's idle timeout (60 seconds) and your application's keep-alive timeout (30 seconds on your instances).

Could you raise the keep-alive timeout on your instances to 75 seconds? That way the load balancer always closes idle connections first. I'll keep the ticket open while we monitor.

Sunita

Six months with Tallybird: an honest review

I switched to Tallybird in March after years of juggling spreadsheets, and for most of that time I would have told anyone who asked that it was the best money app I'd ever used. So please read this whole review before you decide anything, because the ending matters.

First, the good parts, and there are a lot of them. The design is lovely: clean, calm and never cluttered, even with nine accounts connected. Linking all nine bank accounts took one attempt each, and for five months the overnight sync ran so quietly I forgot it existed. Setting up categories took about ten minutes, and the automatic categorisation got smarter every week; by May it was sorting almost all of my transactions correctly without any help. The monthly reports are the best I've seen in any app. I finally understood where our grocery money was going, and we cut that bill by almost a fifth over the spring. Shared budgets with my partner worked perfectly, and the goal tracker genuinely motivated us to pay off a car loan two months early. I've read other reviews complaining about crashes, but in six months I never had a single one, on my phone or my tablet.

There are small niggles. The widget only shows one budget at a time, the dark mode is more grey than dark, and I wish I could split a transaction into more than four parts. The web version also feels like an afterthought next to the phone app. None of that would have stopped me recommending it.

Now the part that matters. In late August, after an update, Tallybird's bank sync ran overnight and deleted every transaction from June, July and August across all nine of my accounts. Three months of categorised history, notes and receipt photos were simply gone. Nothing in the app warned me; I only noticed because the monthly report suddenly showed a summer with no spending at all. The balances were still right, which somehow made it more confusing. I contacted support the same morning. The first reply came eleven days later and asked me to try logging out and back in. By then I had already rebuilt what I could from bank statements.

I've since exported everything that was left and moved our budgeting back to a spreadsheet. I've cancelled my subscription and I won't be renewing. It's genuinely sad, because the app itself is beautifully made. But a budgeting app that can silently wipe three months of data, and a support team that takes eleven days to answer, isn't something I can trust with our finances.

question.instruction: Does the reviewer say they have stopped using the app?

notes: Final paragraph: budgeting moved back to a spreadsheet and the subscription cancelled.

To: Customer Relations, Skyvale Airways
From: Ingrid Castellanos
Date: Thursday 10 September 2026
Re: Suitcase missing since flight SV 482, Lisbon to Oslo, 3 September

Dear Customer Relations,

Let me start with the practical part: if my suitcase has not been delivered by Saturday 12 September, I will file a formal complaint with the national aviation consumer office. I have already drafted it.

Now, I'd like to congratulate Skyvale on a truly memorable holiday. I have spent seven of my ten days in Norway in the same pair of jeans, which I'm told is very on-trend in Oslo this season, so thank you for that.

For the record, my suitcase did not arrive on flight SV 482 on 3 September. At the Oslo baggage desk I queued for forty minutes, filed a report (reference OSL-SV-55821) and was handed a 'comfort kit' containing a toothbrush, a comb and one sachet of shampoo, which I have been rationing ever since. I was told the bag would 'almost certainly' be on the next day's flight. It wasn't. Nor was it on the one after that.

Your baggage tracking page has been a particular delight. For six days it has shown the same status, 'Located, awaiting forwarding', which is a comforting phrase if you don't think about it for more than a second. I have called your helpline four times. The average hold time was 52 minutes, and on two of those calls I was disconnected just as someone picked up. The one agent I did reach, on Monday, promised a call back within 24 hours. I am still waiting for it, which I suppose shows real commitment to consistency.

On day five I received an automated email inviting me to rate my 'overall journey experience' from one to ten. I didn't fill it in, but I admired the optimism.

In the meantime I have spent €146 on clothes, a phone charger and toiletries, and I have kept every receipt. Your online claim form, meanwhile, rejects any photo larger than 1 MB, so I have now photographed the same pharmacy receipt eleven times. I've learned a great deal about image compression this week, which I suppose counts as a cultural experience.

P.S. As I was finishing this letter, a courier knocked on the door of my rental flat with the suitcase. It's a little scuffed, but everything inside seems to be there. I'm sending this letter anyway, because I'd like the €146 reimbursed, and because nobody should have to spend a week chasing a bag.

question.instruction: By the end of the letter, has the writer's suitcase been returned to her?

notes: The P.S. says a courier delivered the suitcase as she finished the letter, contents apparently intact.
